<?php

function bgenerate($n) {
    return str_shuffle(str_repeat('[', $n) . str_repeat(']', $n));
}

function isbalanced($s) {
    $bal = 0;
    for ($i = 0; $i < strlen($s); $i++) {
        if ($s[$i] === '[') {
            $bal++;
        } else {
            $bal--;
        }
        if ($bal < 0) return false;
    }
    return $bal === 0;
}

$tests = [0, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4];

foreach ($tests as $v) {
    $s = bgenerate($v);
    echo "$s\t" . (isbalanced($s) ? 'OK' : 'NOT OK') . PHP_EOL;
}

<?php

function caesarEncode($message, $key) {
    return array_reduce(str_split(strtolower($message)), function($carry, $char) use ($key) {
        $ascii_a = ord('a');
        $ascii_z = ord('z');
        
        if (ord($char) >= $ascii_a && ord($char) <= $ascii_z) {
            $char = chr(((ord($char) - $ascii_a + $key) % 26) + $ascii_a);
        }
        
        return $carry . $char;
    }, '');
}

echo caesarEncode("The quick brown fox Jumped over the lazy Dog", 12), "\n";
?>

Style: functional

<?php

function combinations($n, $k) {
    if ($k === 0) return [[]];
    if ($n < $k) return [];

    $result = [];
    for ($i = 0; $i <= $n - $k; $i++) {
        $head = $i;
        $tailCombinations = combinations($n - $i - 1, $k - 1);
        foreach ($tailCombinations as $combination) {
            array_unshift($combination, $head + 1);
            $result[] = $combination;
        }
    }
    return $result;
}

$n = 5;
$k = 3;
$combinations = combinations($n, $k);

foreach ($combinations as $combination) {
    print_r($combination);
}
?>

def binary_search(array, val, low=0, high=(array.length - 1))
  return nil if high < low
  mid = (low + high) >> 1
  case val <=> array[mid]
    when -1 then binary_search(array, val, low, mid - 1)
    when 1 then binary_search(array, val, mid + 1, high)
    else mid
  end
end

def to_gray(n)
  raise Math::DomainError, "integer is negative" if n < 0
  n ^ (n >> 1)
end

def from_gray(g)
  raise Math::DomainError, "integer is negative" if g < 0
  result = 0
  while g > 0
    result ^= g
    g >>= 1
  end
  result
end

(0..31).each do |number|

instruction: Write a fast ruby implementation of: rosetta — Temperature conversion (ruby). It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input:
Task: Rosetta Code reference — "Temperature conversion" in RUBY. A complete, standard-library-only snippet to copy the idiom and structure of. Source: https://rosettacode.org/wiki/Temperature_conversion
Style: fast
output:
module TempConvert
  FROM_TEMP_SCALE_TO_K = {
    'kelvin'     => ->(t) { t },
    'celsius'    => ->(t) { t + 273.15 },
    'fahrenheit' => ->(t) { (t + 459.67) * 5/9.0 },
    'rankine'    => ->(t) { t * 5/9.0 },
    'delisle'    => ->(t) { 373.15 - t * 2/3.0 },
    'newton'     => ->(t) { t * 100/33.0 + 273.15 },
    'reaumur'    => ->(t) { t * 5/4.0 + 273.15 },
    'roemer'     => ->(t) { (t - 7.5) * 40/21.0 + 273.15 }
  }

  TO_TEMP_SCALE_FROM_K = {
    'kelvin'     => ->(t) { t },
    'celsius'    => ->(t) { t - 273.15 },
    'fahrenheit' => ->(t) { t * 9/5.0 - 459.67 },
    'rankine'    => ->(t) { t * 9/5.0 },
    'delisle'    => ->(t) { (373.15 - t) * 3/2.0 },
    'newton'     => ->(t) { (t - 273.15) * 33/100.0 },
    'reaumur'    => ->(t) { (t - 273.15) * 4/5.0 },
    'roemer'     => ->(t) { (t - 273.15) * 21/40.0 + 7.5 }
  }

  SUPPORTED_SCALES = FROM_TEMP_SCALE_TO_K.keys.join('|')

  def self.method_missing(meth, *args)
    if valid_temperature_conversion?(meth)
      convert_temperature(meth, args[0])
    else
      super
    end
  end

  def self.respond_to_missing?(meth, include_private = false)
    valid_temperature_conversion?(meth) || super
  end

  def self.valid_temperature_conversion?(meth)
    meth.to_s =~ /\A#{SUPPORTED_SCALES}_to_#{SUPPORTED_SCALES}\z/
  end

  def self.convert_temperature(meth, temp)
    from_scale, to_scale = meth.to_s.split('_to_')
    return temp.to_f if from_scale == to_scale
    TO_TEMP_SCALE_FROM_K[to_scale].call(FROM_TEMP_SCALE_TO_K[from_scale].call(temp)).round(2)
  end
end

<?php
// Define the WordCounter class
class WordCounter {
    private $words = [];

    // Constructor
    public function __construct() {
        $this->words = [];
    }

    // Method to count words
    public function countWords($text) {
        $words = explode(' ', $text);
        foreach ($words as $word) {
            $word = strtolower($word);
            if (array_key_exists($word, $this->words)) {
                $this->words[$word]++;
            } else {
                $this->words[$word] = 1;
            }
        }
    }

    // Method to get the top words
    public function getTopWords($num) {
        arsort($this->words);
        return array_slice($this->words, 0, $num);
    }
}

// Define the main function
function main() {
    $text = "Hello world! Hello everyone. Welcome to the word counter.";
    $counter = new WordCounter();
    $counter->countWords($text);
    $topWords = $counter->getTopWords(3);
    foreach ($topWords as $word => $count) {
        echo "Word: " . $word . ", Count: " . $count . "\n";
    }
}

// Run the main function
main();
?>

module Stats
  # Class to represent a word count result
  class WordCountResult
    attr_accessor :word_count, :line_count

    def initialize(word_count, line_count)
      @word_count = word_count
      @line_count = line_count
    end
  end

  # Method to count words and lines from a file
  def count_words_and_lines(file_path)
    word_count = 0
    line_count = 0

    File.foreach(file_path) do |line|
      line_count += 1
      words = line.split
      word_count += words.length
    end

    WordCountResult.new(word_count, line_count)
  end

  # Method to read the input file
  def read_input_file(file_path)
    File.read(file_path)
  end

  # Method to count words and lines from the input file
  def count_words_and_lines_from_input_file(file_path)
    input = read_input_file(file_path)
    lines = input.split("\n")
    word_count = 0
    line_count = lines.length

    lines.each do |line|
      words = line.split
      word_count += words.length
    end

    WordCountResult.new(word_count, line_count)
  end

  # Method to count words and lines from the command line
  def count_words_and_lines_from_command_line
    input = ARGV.join(' ')
    lines = input.split("\n")
    word_count = 0
    line_count = lines.length

    lines.each do |line|
      words = line.split
      word_count += words.length
    end

    WordCountResult.new(word_count, line_count)
  end

  # Method to print the word count result
  def print_word_count_result(result)
    puts "Word count: #{result.word_count}"
    puts "Line count: #{result.line_count}"
  end
end

require 'optparse'

class WordCounter
  def initialize(input)
    @input = input
  end

  def count_words_and_lines
    lines = @input.split("\n")
    word_count = lines.map { |line| line.split(/\s+/).size }.sum
    { words: word_count, lines: lines.size }
  end
end

def main
  parser = OptionParser.new
  parser.banner = "Usage: word-counter.rb [options] FILE"
  options = {}

  parser.on("-h", "--help", "Prints this help message") do
    puts parser
    exit
  end

  begin
    parser.parse!
  rescue OptionParser::InvalidOption => e
    puts e.message
    puts parser
    exit 1
  end

  if ARGV.empty?
    puts "Error: No input file provided."
    puts parser
    exit 1
  end

  input_file = ARGV[0]
  unless File.exist?(input_file)
    puts "Error: File '#{input_file}' not found."
    exit 1
  end

  content = File.read(input_file)
  counter = WordCounter.new(content)
  result = counter.count_words_and_lines
  puts "Word Count: #{result[:words]}"
  puts "Line Count: #{result[:lines]}"
end

main if __FILE__ == $0

instruction: What is VACA's code contract for Swift 5 (single module, swiftc)?

Language: Swift 5 (single module, swiftc) (swift).

backend/src/ai/languageGuidance.ts injects this into the write prompt:
- Standard library ONLY — no SPM dependencies (no Vapor, Alamofire, swift-argument-parser). The whole set is type-checked by `swiftc` alone.
- Entry point: put TOP-LEVEL statements in a file named `main.swift`. The `@main` attribute is FORBIDDEN in `main.swift` — the compiler rejects it with "'main' attribute cannot be used in a module that contains top-level code". Use `@main` ONLY in a file NOT named `main.swift`, and at most once in the whole set.
- NEVER mix the two: if you wrote `@main`, the file must not be `main.swift` and must contain no top-level statements; if the file is `main.swift`, use plain top-level code and no `@main`.

instruction: Write a php program: sort [10, 2, 33, 4]. It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input: Basic sort in php: print the result to standard output.
output:
<?php
const VALUES = [10, 2, 33, 4];

function bubble(array $values): array
{
    $items = $values;
    $count = count($items);
    for ($i = 0; $i < $count; $i++) {
        for ($j = 0; $j < $count - 1 - $i; $j++) {
            if ($items[$j] > $items[$j + 1]) {
                $held = $items[$j];
                $items[$j] = $items[$j + 1];
                $items[$j + 1] = $held;
            }
        }
    }
    return $items;
}

echo implode(',', bubble(VALUES)) . PHP_EOL;

VALUES = [5, 3, 9, 1, 7]

def bubble(values)
  items = values.dup
  loop do
    swapped = false
    (items.length - 1).times do |i|
      if items[i] > items[i + 1]
        items[i], items[i + 1] = items[i + 1], items[i]
        swapped = true
      end
    end
    break unless swapped
  end
  items
end

puts bubble(VALUES).join(',')

instruction: Write a php program: word frequency: the quick brown fox jump. It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input: Medium word-freq in php: several functions and a data structure, printing a deterministic report.
output:
<?php
$TEXT = 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog the fox';

function tokens(string $text): array {
    return preg_split('/\s+/', trim($text));
}

function counts(array $words): array {
    $table = [];
    foreach ($words as $word) {
        $table[$word] = ($table[$word] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
    return $table;
}

function ranked(array $table): array {
    $words = array_keys($table);
    usort($words, function (string $a, string $b) use ($table): int {
        if ($table[$a] === $table[$b]) {
            return strcmp($a, $b);
        }
        return $table[$b] <=> $table[$a];
    });
    return $words;
}

$table = counts(tokens($TEXT));
foreach (array_slice(ranked($table), 0, 4) as $word) {
    printf("%s: %d\n", $word, $table[$word]);
}

instruction: Write a php program: inventory report: bolt. It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input: Medium inventory in php: several functions and a data structure, printing a deterministic report.
output:
<?php
$STOCK = [['bolt', 12, 0.5], ['nut', 40, 0.1], ['washer', 0, 0.05]];

function available(array $stock): array {
    return array_values(array_filter($stock, fn(array $row): bool => $row[1] > 0));
}

function total(array $rows): float {
    $sum = 0.0;
    foreach ($rows as $row) {
        $sum += $row[1] * $row[2];
    }
    return $sum;
}

function report(array $rows): array {
    $lines = [];
    foreach ($rows as $row) {
        $lines[] = sprintf('%-8s %3d x %6.2f = %8.2f', $row[0], $row[1], $row[2], $row[1] * $row[2]);
    }
    return $lines;
}

$rows = available($STOCK);
echo implode("\n", report($rows)), "\n";
printf("total %.2f\n", total($rows));

instruction: Write a php program: sort records: bolt. It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input: Medium sort-records in php: several functions and a data structure, printing a deterministic report.
output:
<?php
$ROWS = [['bolt', 12, 0.5], ['nut', 40, 0.1], ['washer', 0, 0.05]];

function by_value(array $rows): array {
    usort($rows, function (array $a, array $b): int {
        $left = $a[1] * $a[2];
        $right = $b[1] * $b[2];
        if ($left === $right) {
            return strcmp($a[0], $b[0]);
        }
        return $right <=> $left;
    });
    return $rows;
}

function by_name(array $rows): array {
    usort($rows, fn(array $a, array $b): int => strcmp($a[0], $b[0]));
    return $rows;
}

function render(array $rows): string {
    $parts = [];
    foreach ($rows as $row) {
        $parts[] = sprintf('%s(%d)', $row[0], $row[1]);
    }
    return implode(', ', $parts);
}

echo 'value ', render(by_value($ROWS)), "\n";
echo 'name  ', render(by_name($ROWS)), "\n";

input: Medium stack in php: several functions and a data structure, printing a deterministic report.
output:
<?php
class Stack {
    private array $items = [];

    public function push(int $value): void {
        $this->items[] = $value;
    }

    public function pop(): ?int {
        return array_pop($this->items);
    }

    public function peek(): ?int {
        if (count($this->items) === 0) {
            return null;
        }
        return $this->items[count($this->items) - 1];
    }

    public function size(): int {
        return count($this->items);
    }
}

function run(array $ops): array {
    $stack = new Stack();
    $out = [];
    foreach ($ops as $op) {
        $parts = explode(' ', $op);
        if ($parts[0] === 'push') {
            $stack->push((int) $parts[1]);
            $out[] = 'push ' . $parts[1];
        } elseif ($parts[0] === 'pop') {
            $value = $stack->pop();
            $out[] = 'pop ' . ($value === null ? 'none' : (string) $value);
        } else {
            $value = $stack->peek();
            $out[] = 'peek ' . ($value === null ? 'none' : (string) $value);
        }
    }
    return $out;
}

$OPS = ['push 3', 'push 1', 'peek', 'pop', 'push 4', 'pop', 'pop'];
echo implode("\n", run($OPS)), "\n";
echo 'left ', count($OPS) > 0 ? 'ok' : 'empty', "\n";

<?php

bolt,12,0.50
nut,40,0.10
washer,0,0.05";

function parse(string $data): array {
    $lines = array_values(array_filter(explode("\n", trim($data))));
    $header = explode(',', array_shift($lines));
    $rows = array_map(fn(string $line): array => explode(',', $line), $lines);
    return [$header, $rows];
}

function totals(array $header, array $rows): array {
    $out = [];
    for ($i = 1; $i < count($header); $i++) {
        $sum = 0.0;
        foreach ($rows as $row) {
            $sum += is_numeric($row[$i]) ? (float) $row[$i] : 1.0;
        }
        $out[$header[$i]] = $sum;
    }
    return $out;
}

[$header, $rows] = parse($DATA);
echo 'columns ', implode(',', array_slice($header, 1)), "\n";
foreach (totals($header, $rows) as $name => $value) {
    printf("%s: %.2f\n", $name, $value);
}

function words(string $text): array {
    return preg_split('/\s+/', trim($text));
}

function transform(array $words): array {
    return array_map(fn(string $word): string => ucfirst($word), $words);
}

function longest(array $words): string {
    $best = '';
    foreach ($words as $word) {
        if (strlen($word) > strlen($best)) {
            $best = $word;
        }
    }
    return $best;
}

function report(array $words): string {
    return implode(' | ', transform($words));
}

class Stack
  def initialize
    @items = []
  end

  def push(value)
    @items.push(value)
  end

  def pop
    @items.pop
  end

  def peek
    @items.last
  end

  def size
    @items.length
  end
end

def run(stack, ops)
  out = []
  ops.each do |op|
    name, _, argument = op.partition(' ')
    case name
    when 'push'
      stack.push(argument.to_i)
      out << "push #{argument}"
    when 'pop'
      out << "pop #{stack.pop || 'none'}"
    else
      out << "peek #{stack.peek || 'none'}"
    end
  end
  out
end

OPS = ['push 3', 'push 1', 'peek', 'pop', 'push 4', 'pop', 'pop']
puts run(Stack.new, OPS).join("\n")

instruction: Write a ruby program: reverse list [3, 1, 4]. It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input: Medium linked-list in ruby: several functions and a data structure, printing a deterministic report.
output:
Node = Struct.new(:value, :next_node)

VALUES = [3, 1, 4]

def build(values)
  head = nil
  values.reverse_each { |value| head = Node.new(value, head) }
  head
end

def reverse(head)
  previous = nil
  while head
    following = head.next_node
    head.next_node = previous
    previous = head
    head = following
  end
  previous
end

def render(head)
  parts = []
  while head
    parts << head.value.to_s
    head = head.next_node
  end
  parts.join(' -> ')
end

head = build(VALUES)
puts render(head)
puts render(reverse(head))

instruction: Write a ruby program: csv totals: name. It must compile and run on its own, standard library only. Reply with the complete file.
input: Medium csv in ruby: several functions and a data structure, printing a deterministic report.
output:
TABLE = <<~CSV
name,qty,price
bolt,12,0.50
nut,40,0.10
washer,0,0.05
CSV

def parse(data)
  lines = data.split("\n").reject(&:empty?)
  header = lines.shift.split(',')
  rows = lines.map { |line| line.split(',') }
  [header, rows]
end

def numeric?(text)
  Float(text)
  true
rescue ArgumentError
  false
end

def totals(header, rows)
  out = {}
  index = 1
  while index < header.length
    name = header[index]
    out[name] = rows.sum { |row| numeric?(row[index]) ? row[index].to_f : 1.0 }
    index += 1
  end
  out
end

header, rows = parse(TABLE)
puts "columns #{header[1..].join(',')}"
totals(header, rows).each { |name, value| puts format('%s: %.2f', name, value) }

NUMBERS = [6, 11, 12, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19]

def factorise(value)
  out = []
  divisor = 2
  while divisor * divisor <= value
    while (value % divisor).zero?
      out << divisor
      value /= divisor
    end
    divisor += 1
  end
  out << value if value > 1
  out
end

def table(numbers)
  numbers.map { |number| [number, factorise(number)] }
end

table(NUMBERS).each { |number, parts| puts format('%d: %s', number, parts.join(' x ')) }

function generateFibonacci(int $count): array {
    $sequence = [0];
    if ($count === 1) return $sequence;
    $a = 0;
    $b = 1;
    for ($i = 1; $i < $count; ++$i) {
        $next = $a + $b;
        array_push($sequence, $next);
        $a = $b;
        $b = $next;
    }
    return $sequence;
}

function runFibonacci() {

    $fibSequence = generateFibonacci(COUNT);
    echo implode(", ", $fibSequence) . "\n";

# Logic to count lines and words in a text file
import os

def count_lines_and_words(file_path):
    try:
        if not os.path.exists(file_path):
            print('Error: The file does not exist.')
            return 0, 0
        with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
            total_lines = len(lines)
            total_words = sum(len(line.split()) for line in lines if line.strip())
        return total_lines, total_words
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'Unexpected error: {e}')
        raise

require 'csv'
require 'fileutils'

module CsvParser
  def self.parse(file_path)
    begin
      stats = {}
      if File.exist?(file_path) && !File.directory?(file_path)
        CSV.foreach(file_path, headers: true, encoding: 'UTF-8') do |row|
          row.each { |key, value| (stats[key] ||= []) << value }
        end
        return stats unless stats.empty?
      else
        puts "ERROR: Unable to open '#{file_path}' for parsing."
      rescue StandardError => e
        puts "ERROR: Parsing failed for #{file_path} - #{e.message}"
      end
    end

    { success: false, error: 'Parse failed' }
  end
end

output: const boardSize = 8;const pieces = [];let currentPlayer = 'red';function initBoard() {const board = document.getElementById('board');board.innerHTML = '';for (let row = 0; row < boardSize; row++) {for (let col = 0; col < boardSize; col++) {const cell = document.createElement('div');cell.className = 'cell';cell.dataset.row = row;cell.dataset.col = col;if ((row < 3 && (row + col) % 2 === 1) || (row > 4 && (row + col) % 2 === 1)) {cell.textContent = '○';cell.classList.add(currentPlayer);} else if ((row === 3 && (row + col) % 2 === 1) || (row === 4 && (row + col) % 2 === 1)) {cell.textContent = ' ';} else {cell.textContent = ' ';}cell.onclick = handleCellClick;board.appendChild(cell);}}const pieces = document.querySelectorAll('.cell');for (const piece of pieces) {const row = parseInt(piece.dataset.row);const col = parseInt(piece.dataset.col);if (piece.textContent === '○') {pieces.push({row,col,color:currentPlayer,selected:false});}}}function handleCellClick(e) {const row = parseInt(e.target.dataset.row);const col = parseInt(e.target.dataset.col);const piece = pieces.find(p => p.row === row && p.col === col);if (piece) {if (piece.selected) {piece.selected = false;e.target.classList.remove('selected');} else {pieces.forEach(p => p.selected = false);const selectedPiece = pieces.find(p => p.row === row && p.col === col);if (selectedPiece) {selectedPiece.selected = true;e.target.classList.add('selected');}}}}function resetGame() {const board = document.getElementById('board');board.innerHTML = '';initBoard();currentPlayer = 'red';}
